title: Research Areas
text:
My research develops statistical and machine learning methods for the physical sciences. The methods come first: time series decomposition, signal extraction from high-noise data, and hybrid statistical and machine learning forecasting. Air quality, floods, groundwater, volcanoes, and climate-related hazards are the applications, and recent work brings the same methods into business analytics education. Publications often belong to several areas, and every count below links to the filtered publication list.

title: Leadership & Service
text: Dr. Tsakiri chairs the Department of Information & Operations at the Norm Brodsky College of Business, Rider University, and is the founding director of its Risk Management and Insurance Certificate Program. This page gives the shape of that work rather than the full record; a full record is available on request.

title: Leadership & Service
text:
Department leadership
As chair of a multidisciplinary department spanning Business Analytics, Information Technology Management, and Supply Chain Management, she is responsible for academic planning, faculty recruitment, mentoring and evaluation, teaching assignments and scheduling, the departmental budget, and the department’s part in the college’s accreditation by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB).

title: Leadership & Service
text:
Curriculum and program development
She has led revisions of the undergraduate analytics and information technology curricula, designed new courses, and built experiential learning into the programs through practicum courses, internships, cooperative education, and industry-sponsored projects. She has also developed interdisciplinary certificate programs for undergraduate and graduate students.

title: Leadership & Service
text:
Program and certificate leadership
As founding director of the Risk Management and Insurance Certificate Program, she designed its curriculum, launched the program, chairs its industry advisory council, recruits and supports the faculty who teach in it, and organizes the events that connect students with practitioners. The certificate is open to Rider undergraduates in any major.

title: Leadership & Service
text:
Students and mentorship
Her work with students includes retention and career-readiness initiatives, co-organizing the college’s annual DataFest competition with industry sponsors, and networking events that bring analytics faculty and students together. She has supervised doctoral and master’s research in the United States, the United Kingdom, and Greece, guided undergraduate research projects in insurance modeling, financial time series, health data, and air quality, and designed and co-directed a conference theme on natural hazards prediction for a sectional meeting of the Geological Society of America.

title: Leadership & Service
text:
Committee service
At Rider she serves on curriculum and assessment committees and has served on faculty search committees and a first-year experience task force. Earlier in her career she was course leader for a master’s program in data analytics and led a statistics group at a university in the United Kingdom, coordinated a cooperation agreement between universities in the United Kingdom and Greece, and served on a program review committee in the United States.

title: Leadership & Service
text:
Teaching
Two decades of statistics and analytics teaching, from introductory statistics to graduate courses in machine learning and business analytics with AI, in business, mathematics, and engineering departments in the United States and the United Kingdom. The course list is on the About page.

title: About
text:
Dr. Katerina G. Tsakiri is a computational statistician and data scientist specializing in machine learning and AI methods for the physical sciences. Her expertise covers time series decomposition, signal extraction from high-noise data, neural networks, and hybrid statistical and machine learning forecasting models, with applications in atmospheric science, hydrology, volcanology, and climate-related hazards. She has developed novel methodologies and tools, including the R package sima for detecting weak signals in environmental monitoring data, and her recent work integrates classical time series techniques with modern machine learning approaches. She is passionate about interdisciplinary training of the next generation of data scientists, using AI in teaching and research.
She is Associate Professor of Management Science and Chair of the Department of Information & Operations at the Norm Brodsky College of Business, Rider University, and Founding Director of Rider’s Risk Management and Insurance Certificate Program. In 2026 she co-authored the book R for Earth and Sustainability Data Analytics with Dr. Antonios E. Marsellos.
